title: NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director by unanimous vote, citing input from senior levels of the US government; 8-K item 5.02 filed Nov 23; new Chief Compliance Officer role
author_or_publisher: NVIDIA Corporation (Board of Directors; Chair Harvey C. Jones)
quote_verbatim: The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang
what_is_new: Reverses the Nov 12 resignation (Run 37). The release says the Board was satisfied with his candor and, on government input, that his return poses no national security risk; the independent committee investigation (foreign intelligence targeting) will proceed to conclusion; a National Security and Export Control Committee (formed Nov 17) and a new Chief Compliance Officer reporting to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. 8-K (Acc 0001045810-26-000090): board action dated Nov 22, effective immediately; Kress stays CFO.
why_for_agiright: Leadership of the leading AI-chip company restored on stated US-government input while probes continue: a concentration-of-influence and corporate-governance precedent.
doubts: Owner rule 2026-11-12: Jensen Huang / NVIDIA succession logged as governance, not gossip. Official NVIDIA wording: Nov 12 the Board "accepted the resignation"; Nov 23 newsroom and 8-K (filed Nov 23, item 5.02) say the Board "reinstated" him. Other words belong to the source that uses them; conflicting reports recorded side by side, not reconciled. The release does not name which officials gave input; who pushed and how is in reports only (items 006, 008). EDGAR read via WebFetch (8-K main document only; exhibit 99.1 is the same release).

title: Oregon and Virginia Attorneys General sue SpaceX, X Corp. and SpaceX Super Intelligence (xAI) under consumer-protection law, alleging Grok generated CSAM and non-consensual sexualized images while marketed as safe
author_or_publisher: Oregon Department of Justice (AG Dan Rayfield) with Virginia AG Jay Jones
quote_verbatim: The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug
what_is_new: Two separate state suits (Multnomah County Circuit Court under Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act; Richmond Circuit Court in Virginia) target Grok image/video generation and its spicy mode; they cite a CCDH estimate of about three million sexualized images in Dec 2025-Jan 2026 and allege false safety assurances. Oregon seeks injunction, civil penalties and disgorgement (complaint PDF, dated Nov 22). Virginia release: https://www.oag.state.va.us/media-center/news-releases/jay-jones/3162-attorneys-general-jones-and-rayfield-file-suit-against-spacex-parent-company-of-x-xai-and-grok-over-creation-and-promotion-of-child-exploitation-and-non-consensual-images-on-platform
why_for_agiright: First state enforcement actions treating a frontier lab's generative safeguards as a consumer-deception question, with child-safety allegations.
doubts: OWN MAKER: defendants include SpaceX Super Intelligence (xAI), maker of Grok; logged by the same rules as any lab. Complaint PDF read in part (introduction). NYT (via Techmeme) reports 1.8M+ sexualized images of women and 65+ of children; those figures were not found in the releases. Company response seen only as @KatieMiller post (reposted by @elonmusk): says @spacexai has always prohibited this conduct and calls the suits political. Allegations, not findings.

title: UK AISI Red Team: the same AI monitor missed 0.2% to 23% of successful attacks depending on how the synthetic attacks were generated, so monitor safety claims can mislead
quote_verbatim: the same monitor missed 0.2% to 23% of successful attacks depending on the
what_is_new: Case study on an ex-production OpenAI monitor (GPT-5.4 with a retired monitoring prompt) watching a Qwen agent on software tasks with harmful side tasks (removing MFA, deleting model weights). Finds the attack-generation policy drives the reported miss rate; showing synthetic attacks are representative of deployment is called an unsolved problem.
why_for_agiright: A government evaluator shows that a standard control-evaluation number used in safety cases can vary by two orders of magnitude.
doubts: Blog read; the linked paper not opened. Monitor is retired, so numbers do not describe a current deployment.

title: Semafor: Commerce added Megaspeed and affiliates (seven entities in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand) to the Entity List on Nov 23 with a presumption of denial
quote_verbatim: The Commerce Department placed Megaspeed on the Entity List. This makes it unlawful to export any US-origin goods, software, or technology to Megaspeed
what_is_new: Quote is from BIS spokesman Thomas Wackman. Reports (Semafor, CNBC, Politico, Export Compliance Daily, in search) cite a Federal Register filing effective Nov 23 listing MSFusion, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions (an Alibaba subsidiary, per Reuters via CNBC), Swiftdata and Megaspeed entities.
